data.title: BofA favours 'risk-off' for November; reasons go beyond midterm elections
data.description:
Bank of America sees little reason for investors to rush back into stocks ahead of November.

Strategist Michael Hartnett favours a defensive stance because of a combination of stubbornly high borrowing costs, geopolitical tensions, election uncertainty and cracks in the AI trade.

His warning extends beyond who controls Congress – several forces supporting corporate earnings and stock valuations are coming under pressure simultaneously.

Higher yields leave stocks facing tougher competition

Hartnett expects the Fed to raise interest rates again on October 28, arguing that policymakers need to rebuild confidence in their inflation fight.

High yields create two problems for stocks: they raise financing costs and make bonds much more competitive with equities. That’s significant given businesses dependent on refinancing or distant profits face particular pressure.

Yet Hartnett also sees a potential release valve.

A credible tightening move could lower longer-term Treasury yields by another 20bps, potentially cushioning stocks if investors become more confident that inflation will retreat.

Higher oil prices threaten margins and household spending

Oil is another reason BofA remains cautious, with conflicts involving the Middle East and Ukraine complicating the outlook for energy supplies.

Hartnett identifies these geopolitical pressures as a key threat alongside interest rates and election uncertainty, especially since the economic implications reach well beyond petrol stations.

Persistently expensive energy can significantly squeeze transport and manufacturing margins, while leaving households with less money for discretionary purchases.

For investors, this means a difficult combination: weaker spending power and insufficient inflation relief.

Simply put, companies may struggle to pass higher costs through to customers, while central banks have less room to support demand.

A democratic sweep could unsettle policy expectations

Hartnett also flags the growing possibility of Democrats capturing both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterms.

His concern centres on a potentially decisive result that could force investors to reassess the policy assumptions embedded in asset prices.

Election probabilities, however, remain market expectations rather than confirmed outcomes, and congressional control alone cannot determine subsequent legislation.

The immediate investment risk is repricing. Businesses and investors could delay decisions while assessing the balance of power and the scope for policy changes.

That uncertainty adds another obstacle for a market already wrestling with expensive capital and uneven confidence.

AI financing worries challenge a major market engine

The fourth concern strikes at a central source of market enthusiasm: artificial intelligence.

Investors are scrutinizing whether heavily financed infrastructure expansion can generate returns quickly enough to justify its costs.

CoreWeave’s shares were heading for a weekly decline exceeding 22% on October 16, as concerns about borrowing and interest rates weighed on the AI infrastructure trade.

The broader implication is that strong demand alone may no longer satisfy shareholders. Financing terms, cash generation and repayment capacity increasingly matter.

Pressure across both AI stocks and credit markets suggests investors are demanding stronger evidence that expansion can become financially sustainable.

Where BofA sees opportunities despite the caution

Hartnett’s defensive stance still leaves room for selective exposure.

He favours potential beneficiaries of peaking bond yields, including small cap stocks, real estate investment trusts (REITs) and the consumer discretionary sector.

These areas could gain breathing room if longer-term borrowing costs decline.

That makes the recommendation more nuanced than a blanket call to abandon equities.

The opportunity depends partly on the source of any yield decline: improving inflation confidence would offer a healthier backdrop than a sharp deterioration in growth.

For November, the key question is whether lower yields can ease financial pressure while confidence in corporate earnings and AI investment holds together.

data.title: DJT stock flashes a warning sign as Trump Media risks build
data.description:
Trump Media stock continued its strong downward trend, reaching its lowest level on record as headwinds jumped. DJT fell to $6.9, down by 60% from its highest point this year and 33% below its highest point in August. This sell-off may continue as the company faces some major headwinds.

Trump Media is facing headwinds

DJT stock has continued its strong downward trend this month as the company faces major headwinds. One of them is that President Donald Trump’s approval rating has continued to fall because of the rising inflation. A report released this week showed that the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.7% in September. Core inflation rose 2.7% last month.

Trump’s approval rate has plunged to a record low, with his net approval moving to minus 27. 34% of the voters approve his work, while 61% of them disapprove. Trump is being opposed by Republicans, Democrats, and Independents because of his corruption and the ongoing US-Iran war.

The ongoing approval rating drop is also affecting traffic to the Truth Social website. SimilarWeb data shows that the website had 15.31 million visits in September. While this increase was an 11% monthly jump, it remains much lower than its competitors. For example, X and Reddit had 4.18 billion and 3.82 billion, respectively.

Trump Media is also not making money. The most recent results showed that it made a net loss of $238 million in the June quarter and $643 million in the first six months of the year. Large advertisers have stayed away from Truth Social, while the recently launched API solution will not make it a lot of money in the long term.

DJT stock has also slumped because Bitcoin has lost momentum. Bitcoin has dropped from a high of $87,000 earlier this month to the current $81,000. Trump Media is the 10th-largest Bitcoin holder in the world, with 12,062 coins. Its coins are now valued at $977 million.

Trump Media is also highly overvalued, considering that it has not made money at the peak of Trump’s presidency. A $2 billion valuation for a company losing substantial sums of money per quarter is quite expensive.

DJT stock technicals point to more downside 

Trump Media stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Trump Media stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has dropped from $10.56  in August to the current $6.99. 

The stock has dropped below the 50-day moving average. It has also formed an inverted cup-and-handle pattern, a common continuation sign. 

DJT stock’s Average Directional Index (ADX) has risen to 21, its highest point 21, its highest point since August. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of $5. A drop below that level will point to further downside, towards $3.

data.title: Strategy stock (MSTR) falls as MSCI index exclusion threatens passive investments
data.description:
Strategy (formerly known as MicroStrategy) stock (MSTR) fell on Friday as investors assessed the potential removal of the Bitcoin treasury company from MSCI's global equity indexes, despite a rise in Bitcoin prices.

The company also announced plans to maintain a 12% annualised dividend rate on its STRC preferred stock for November, subject to shareholder approval and related amendments taking effect.

Strategy shares declined 6% on Friday, while Bitcoin traded around $82,290, having gained more than 1.3% over the previous 24 hours.

Strategy, led by Michael Saylor, is the world's largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with 848,250 BTC.

The stock's decline highlights how factors beyond cryptocurrency prices, including index inclusion and financing costs, can influence investor sentiment towards the company.

MSCI rules put Strategy's index inclusion at risk

MSCI said on Thursday that non-operating companies would be ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30.

The index provider plans to publish the final list of affected companies on November 11.

Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet are among the companies potentially facing removal.

SharpLink and several other cryptocurrency treasury companies are on a watchlist for possible exclusion.

The policy follows a review that MSCI began last year into whether digital asset treasury companies resemble investment funds, which are already excluded from its indexes.

MSCI deferred its original proposal in January before broadening the review to cover non-operating companies more generally.

The potential exclusion matters because passive funds tracking MSCI benchmarks are required to hold constituent stocks.

Strategy previously warned that removal could lead to $2.8 billion worth of its shares being liquidated.

Strategy has disputed MSCI's proposed classification. In a statement on Friday, the company said, “We believe the proposal is misguided.”

Strategy also argued that MSCI's distinction between operating and non-operating companies was undefined and lacked a basis in US GAAP, IFRS or recognised legal frameworks.

The company said funds tracking MSCI's Global Investable Market Indexes held just 3.1% of its outstanding shares, potentially limiting the direct impact of an exclusion.

Strategy maintains 12% STRC dividend rate

Separately, Strategy's board declared daily cash dividends on its STRC preferred stock for each calendar day in November, subject to shareholder approval and the effectiveness of related amendments.

The annualised dividend rate will remain at 12%.

Strategy said management would continue recommending that rate until STRC demonstrates “sustained, healthy trading near $100 per share.”

Payments are scheduled to begin on November 2, with each dividend payable on the business day following its record date, according to a regulatory filing.

STRC is one of Strategy's key fundraising instruments for Bitcoin purchases.

Daily dividend payments could help make the preferred stock more attractive to investors and support trading around its $100 par value.

STRC was down 0.2% at $99.33.

Bitcoin purchases and financing strategy in focus

Strategy added 250 Bitcoin for $21.5 million last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC.

During the week ending October 4, the company repurchased $176 million worth of STRC, spending more than six times as much on the buybacks as on its $28 million in Bitcoin purchases.

The company introduced a capital framework on June 29 that allows it to sell Bitcoin to fund dividend payments.

It also raised STRC's annual dividend rate to 12% at the time.

Strategy's business model relies on raising capital through stock and debt sales to acquire Bitcoin.

While that approach has made the company a major proxy for cryptocurrency exposure in equity markets, its shares remain sensitive to financing conditions and index-related developments.

Index-related risks like MSCI’s proposed exclusion are closely watched by traders who follow stock reactions through top online trading platforms.

data.title: Jordan is driving Nike's resale volume growth: buy NKE stock?
data.description:
Nike’s (NKE) Jordan brand is gaining ground among sneaker resellers, offering an “encouraging” signal for a business still struggling to regain its footing.

Citi’s tracking showed Nike captured 72.3% of resale volume in September, a 63bps increase from August, with Jordan driving most of the improvement.

That also exceeded the 70.8% average recorded between June and August.

Still, investors should resist treating stronger resale share as proof of a financial recovery. For NKE stock, these latest figures support cautious optimism about brand appeal rather than an immediate buying case.

What Jordan’s resale volume means for Nike stock

The most important distinction is between resale market share and actual sales growth.

Nike could capture a larger portion of secondary-market transactions even if the overall market contracts.

Citi’s reported figures alone therefore cannot establish whether more Nike sneakers changed hands in September, whether resale prices strengthened, or whether sellers earned better returns.

Those details matter since frequent trading doesn’t necessarily showcase stronger pricing power.

A coveted shoe commanding a premium tells investors something different from an oversupplied model changing hands at a discount.

September’s share also remained 4.7 percentage points below the 77.0% peak recorded in October 2023.

The improvement deserves attention, but it falls short of demonstrating that NKE has restored its former secondary-market dominance.

In short, resale transactions themselves don’t really establish an increase in the firm’s reported revenue.

Nike is deliberately accepting pain at Jordan

There is nevertheless a credible bullish interpretation – Jordan retains “consumer relevance” while Nike works to repair its distribution strategy.

On its latest earnings call, management acknowledged oversupplying iconic Jordan retro products and outlined plans to reduce the volume and frequency of selected launches.

Jordan represented 13% of NKE’s global business in Q1, while its sales declined in the mid-teens.

The investment logic is that tighter supply may eventually restore exclusivity, reduce the need for discounts, and improve the economics of future releases.

However, September’s resale share does not prove that this strategy is already succeeding.

Plus, Nike also faces a difficult trade-off: selling fewer pairs can protect a franchise’s desirability while hurting near-term revenue.

Investors buying the turnaround must accept that healthier brand positioning and faster sales growth may arrive on different schedules.

NKE shares need a strong earnings case

All in all, there’s reason to remain cautious on NKE shares; Jordan’s resale improvement is insufficient reason to load up on them today.

There sure are encouraging operating signs. Nike's performance portfolio grew at a high-single-digit rate in the first quarter, while gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 42.8%.

Yet management still projected a high-single-digit revenue decline for fiscal 2027 – underscoring how heavily the weaker businesses weigh on the recovery.

For shareholders, the decisive issue is how much “sustainable profit” Nike Inc can generate while resetting Jordan, Sportswear and Greater China; and a resale-share gain offers rather limited help in answering that valuation question.

data.title: Oil set for weekly gain as supply constraints keep prices elevated
data.description:
Oil prices held steady on Friday as uncertainty over Middle Eastern supplies continued to support the market, with no immediate resolution to the conflict in sight.

Brent crude futures traded around $105.8, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude stood at $97.71. Both benchmarks remained on course for weekly gains, with WTI up 6% and Brent rising roughly 1% over the week.

Reports that Washington was considering easing restrictions on some sanctioned oil tankers, alongside the International Energy Agency's (IEA) pledge to release the remaining 100 million barrels under its coordinated supply agreement, provided some support to market sentiment.

However, persistent supply concerns and escalating security risks in the Middle East continued to keep prices elevated.

US considers easing restrictions on oil tankers

Washington is reportedly considering lifting sanctions on some vessels belonging to the so-called shadow fleet, which transports oil from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela.

The move is aimed at easing pressure on oil transportation and curbing rising freight rates, offering a possible route to improving the flow of crude into global markets.

The IEA's planned release of the remaining 100 million barrels under its supply agreement has also helped sentiment, as governments seek to offset disruptions and improve the availability of oil.

However, these developments have done little to eliminate concerns about the durability of global supplies. Even with production and exports recovering toward pre-war levels in recent weeks, rising attacks around the region's critical shipping routes have renewed fears of further interruptions.

Strait of Hormuz remains key risk

The biggest source of pressure continues to be the Middle East, where attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial vessels are increasing transportation costs and adding to the risk premium built into oil prices.

Iran said Friday that it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States left the region. The statement comes as attacks around the vital waterway have increased over the past 10 days.

Iran has said the escalation in strikes is a response to the US blockade of its ports. The continuing confrontation has left traders uncertain about how reliably oil can move through the Gulf.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global energy shipments, and further disruption could tighten supplies and push prices higher.

The prospect of further attacks means that even barrels continuing to leave the Gulf carry an additional security premium, keeping prices elevated despite efforts to improve supply availability.

Storm loading after calm?

William Blair energy research analyst Neal Dingmann has warned that the market could face a further sharp spike in prices.

He told Yahoo Finance on Friday that major energy executives were concerned about the possibility of a so-called "super spike" if supply disruptions intensified.

Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones has also warned that crude prices may not have reached their peak, arguing that unresolved geopolitical risks leave room for another sharp increase.

"I'm long oil, bullish on oil. I think it can rally another $20 or $25," Jones told CNBC.

With not much headway in the Middle East conflicts, oil prices seem set to stay elevated at least in the near term.

data.title: Palantir stock reverses after hitting key resistance: is it a good buy?
data.description:
Palantir stock has suffered a big reversal, wiping out some of the gains made since June when it bottomed at $106.5. It dropped to $186.7, down by 12.75% from its highest point this year. Still, analysts are optimistic about the company, citing its strong fundamentals and revenue growth.

Palantir stock coincided with the tech sector sell-off

The ongoing PLTR stock sell-off has coincided with that of most software companies. Salesforce dropped to $241.4, down by 10% from its highest point in September. Other top software companies like Palo Alto Networks, Twilio, Okta, Fastly, and SentinelOne were among the top laggards.

One reason for the ongoing Palantir stock retreat is the upcoming midterm elections, where Democrats are set to win the House of Representatives and, potentially, the Senate. 

Analysts predict that a win by Democrats will lead to some major investigations on companies that have helped the administration on key issues. Palantir will be targeted for its role in helping the administration in border issues. It is unclear whether these investigations will impact its revenue and profitability growth.

Analysts are bullish on PLTR stock

Still, on the positive side, analysts are highly bullish on PLTR stock, citing its strong revenue and profitability growth. On Thursday, Mizuho analysts boosted the target from $215 to $245. Two days before that, Baird analysts set the target price at $250, while Barclays initiated with a target of $265. Other analysts who have maintained a bullish outlook for the stock are from Goldman Sachs, Raymond James, and UBS.

Most of these analysts are citing the company’s revenue and profitability growth. The most recent results showed that Palantir’s business continued doing well in the second quarter, driven by corporate and government orders.

American companies are increasingly turning to Palantir’s solutions, with the revenue rising by 149%. Their remaining deal value jumped to $6.24 billion, with more firms embracing its AIP solution. 

In total, Palantir’s revenue rose 93% YoY to $1.93 billion, while the adjusted income from operations rose to $1.19 billion. The management expects that this revenue growth will continue in the foreseeable future. 

Its third-quarter revenue is expected to be between $2.16 billion and $2.164 billion, much higher than the $1.18 billion it made last year.

READ MORE: Palantir stock is surging: will it retest its all-time high or reverse?

Palantir’s key valuation multiple, known as the Rule of 40, shows that it is highly undervalued. This multiple is calculated by adding a company’s revenue growth with its margins. In this case, adding the two gives PLTR a multiple of 155%, one of the highest in the US.

Traditional metrics, however, show that it is highly overvalued. It has a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 123, much higher than the sector median of 21.8. This multiple is much higher than other software companies like Microsoft, Salesforce, and Okta.

Palantir stock price analysis

PLTR stock chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that the PLTR stock rebounded from $106 in June to a high of $212 in this month. Its highest point was notable because it coincided with the highest point in November last year. It has also formed a bearish engulfing pattern, where a big bearish candle covers a bullish candle fully.

Therefore, the stock will likely retreat further, potentially to $160, and then resume the upward trend. If this happens, the stock will likely jump to $250.

data.title: Evening digest: oil hits $110, Tesla unveils Roadster
data.description:
Oil prices climbed above $110 a barrel as escalating geopolitical tensions raised concerns about global supply, while gold headed for a weekly loss amid expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes.

Tesla shares fell after the company unveiled its redesigned Roadster, while Apple stock edged higher following strong initial demand for its first foldable iPhone.

Oil prices hit $110 as supply concerns intensify

Brent crude rose 3.7% to $110 a barrel, its highest level since May, as traders grew concerned about the prospect of prolonged supply disruptions and diminishing chances of near-term relief.

WTI crude rose 3.24% to above $101.

Iran-backed Houthi rebels continued missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, while Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks on energy infrastructure.

Reports of a warning over potential danger in Saudi Arabia's Khamis Mushait added to concerns surrounding major energy export centres.

Uncertainty also surrounded a proposed Russian diesel release.

US lawmakers introduced a bipartisan bill to block President Donald Trump's deal with Moscow, which would allow Russia to release several hundred million barrels of diesel.

However, continued exclusion of Russian diesel from global markets could force refineries elsewhere to increase processing to meet demand.

A recent attack on Russia's Ryazan refinery, which reportedly halted a primary processing unit, further complicated the outlook.

Crude prices have risen more than 70% this year amid disruptions linked to the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflicts.

European diesel futures have more than doubled, reflecting tightness in refined-product markets.

Gold heads for weekly loss as rate-hike bets rise

Gold prices were largely steady on Friday but remained on track for a weekly decline as stronger-than-expected US inflation data increased expectations of further monetary tightening.

Spot gold fell 0.04% to $4,168.73 an ounce, leaving it down 0.59% for the week. US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.51% higher at $4,191.10 an ounce, which is at 0.59% weekly decline.

US producer prices recorded their largest increase in four and a half years in September, following data showing consumer prices accelerated during the month.

Federal Reserve officials offered mixed signals on the outlook.

Chair Kevin Warsh expressed optimism about the US economy but did not indicate the likely direction of interest rates.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee described the inflation data as discouraging, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned that worsening inflation expectations could require more aggressive rate increases.

Traders largely expect the Fed to hold rates this month but are pricing in a 90% probability of a December hike, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

Higher interest rates tend to weigh on gold because the metal does not pay interest.

Tesla stock falls after Roadster unveiling

Tesla shares fell nearly 3% on Friday after the company showcased a redesigned Roadster featuring thrusters developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

The demonstration included the vehicle performing aerial manoeuvres, jumping over obstacles and accelerating from zero to 60 miles per hour in less than a second, according to Tesla's presentation.

However, production is now targeted for 2028, compared with the original 2020 delivery goal announced in 2017.

Tesla has not disclosed pricing or specifications for other performance variants.

Analysts questioned the car's potential financial contribution given its expected low production volumes.

Gary Black of The Future Fund estimated that 3,000 annual deliveries and a $100,000 profit per vehicle could add approximately $0.06 per share to Tesla's 2029 adjusted earnings.

The Roadster could nevertheless strengthen Tesla's technology-focused brand as the company prioritises autonomous driving and robotics.

Apple shares rise after foldable iPhone sells out

Apple shares edged up on Friday after its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, reportedly sold out shortly after preorders opened.

Social media users reported that estimated delivery dates had shifted from October 23 to late January, suggesting initial demand was exceeding available supply.

The device features a 5.4-inch external display and a 7.6-inch foldable internal screen.

Apple expects foldable smartphones to account for roughly 10% of the market by 2029.

Separately, Apple Chairman Tim Cook said Apple Intelligence had received regulatory clearance in China, with a test rollout expected later in October.

The company has partnered with Alibaba to use its Qwen AI models in mainland China.

Apple is also working with Meta to optimise its Muse Spark open-weight AI model for high-end Mac computers.

Despite the developments, some analysts remain cautious about iPhone demand, with UBS maintaining a Neutral rating and KeyBanc retaining an Underweight rating.

data.title: Micron stock continues slump, analysts are saying it's a buying opportunity
data.description:
Micron Technology shares MU fell about 4% on Friday, taking the weekly decline to 10% as investors assessed the potential threat from China’s memory-chip industry and concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

The stock has retreated from its summer peak of more than $1,200, despite having more than tripled this year.

The recent sell-off followed progress reported by Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) on a denser dynamic random access memory (DRAM) architecture known as 4F-squared.

The design could allow manufacturers to fit more memory cells into a smaller area, potentially improving production economics.

CXMT has also indicated plans to introduce server-memory products using the technology by the end of 2026, prompting concerns that Chinese suppliers could eventually expand their presence in the market.

However, analysts argue that the development does not necessarily threaten Micron’s position in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), a specialised technology used in AI servers.

CXMT’s breakthrough raises concerns about competition

Micron and South Korea’s SK Hynix both fell sharply after CXMT’s announcement.

By Friday, October 16, Micron had lost around 10% for the week, while SK Hynix was down nearly 15%.

The market reaction reflects concerns that advances in Chinese memory manufacturing could increase supply and put pressure on prices.

However, progress in chip design does not automatically translate into competitive mass production.

Citi analysts said CXMT’s manufacturing process remained several generations behind industry leaders.

They estimated that mass production using the new architecture was unlikely before 2028, potentially giving Micron and SK Hynix time to advance their own technologies.

The possibility of additional supply remains a concern, particularly if Chinese manufacturers eventually expand production enough to affect industry pricing.

Analysts see limited immediate threat to AI memory demand

Fundstrat vice president for market intelligence Kent Fung said CXMT’s new architecture could challenge conventional server DRAM but did not directly compete with the HBM products required for AI servers.

“Investors should consider the possibility that the knee-jerk response to CXMT’s announcement has been a bit of an overreaction,” Fung wrote in a research note on Thursday.

He added that CXMT’s breakthrough had a weaker connection to AI and therefore potentially weaker implications for memory and storage stocks’ growth prospects.

The distinction matters because conventional DRAM serves computers and servers more broadly, while HBM is designed to move data rapidly to AI processors.

CXMT’s progress in conventional memory does not establish that it can immediately challenge the advanced HBM products supplied by Micron and SK Hynix.

Micron’s fiscal 2026 annual report also said AI-driven memory demand was outpacing industry supply, supporting stronger pricing and margins.

Rising memory prices support Micron’s investment case

KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reiterated a $1,750 price target on Micron and described it as one of his favourite investment ideas following a trip to assess Asian supply chains.

Vinh said DRAM prices in the fourth quarter were expected to rise by 15% to 20% from the previous quarter. He also noted that Google was considering extending long-term memory-supply agreements through 2035.

While Vinh said he did not expect the current memory upcycle to last until 2031 or 2035, he argued that the potential agreements suggested customers were concerned about shortages persisting beyond 2028.

These expectations offer support for Micron’s outlook, although the potential for increased competition remains a risk.

If Chinese suppliers add meaningful capacity, additional supply could weaken memory prices and reduce the returns earned on new factories.

Even without an immediate loss of AI customers, investors could become less willing to pay premium valuations for earnings that may be unusually strong near the peak of a memory-chip cycle.

The outlook therefore depends not only on AI demand but also on how quickly supply expands and how that affects pricing.

data.title: CoreWeave stock drops nearly 20% this week. Why analysts say its a buy
data.description:
CoreWeave stock CRWV fell again on Friday after recovering in the previous session, putting the AI cloud computing company on track for a steep weekly loss as investors continued to worry about its debt-financed expansion amid rising borrowing costs.

The stock dropped about 7.2% on Friday, even as the S&P 500 edged higher.

Nasdaq Composite opened lower by about 0.4%.

CoreWeave shares have lost nearly 20% this week as concerns over inflation, interest rates and the financing requirements of artificial intelligence infrastructure weighed on sentiment.

In addition, Gartner released research indicating that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will most likely cease independent operations.

Rising borrowing costs put debt under scrutiny

For some analysts, CoreWeave has become a symbol of the debt-fuelled AI infrastructure boom, in which companies are committing billions of dollars to data centres and computing capacity before the long-term returns on that investment are fully established.

The sell-off intensified after hotter-than-expected US inflation data on Wednesday heightened concerns that interest rates could remain elevated, increasing the cost of financing capital-intensive AI infrastructure.

Nicholas Mugalli, chief investment officer at World Trade Securities, said CoreWeave short sellers made around $806 million in paper profit on Wednesday when the stock fell 15.5%.

CoreWeave's $2.8 billion of 9.75% bonds issued in April traded at 79.5 cents on the dollar on Thursday, yielding more than 15%, according to data provided by BondCliQ.

The loss-making cloud computing company has about $50 billion in debt.

"A hot inflation print triggered a ​sharp selloff in CoreWeave because its business model is a highly indebted play on future data center demand," BCA Research analysts said.

"Although the rest ​of the tech complex is also sensitive to the ​pace and magnitude of AI adoption and use, it is, on average, ‌considerably ⁠less sensitive to interest rates"

CoreWeave rents out Nvidia graphics processing units and supplies computing power to AI laboratories such as OpenAI and major technology companies including Meta Platforms.

It operates data centres across the US and internationally.

The business depends on continued demand for computing capacity, while its expansion requires substantial upfront investment.

That combination has left investors weighing the strength of its contracted revenue against the risks associated with its debt and future capital expenditure.

Why neoclouds face a threat, but CoreWeave is likely to survive

Gartner said in 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030, but enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period.

A cumulative $8.5 trillion in revenue would be required to recover the massive AI spend, according to Gartner; however, total enterprise and consumer AI revenue that can be attributed to AI data centers during this period is forecast to reach no more than $3.6 trillion, it said.

"Failure to achieve sustainable ROIC on rapidly depreciating assets would almost certainly necessitate write-downs," it said.

Neoclouds will be among the most exposed to the imbalance between revenue and capital spending, and cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations, it said.

Melvin, Milk Road analyst, agreed but said CoreWeave and Nebius will be the top survivors.

"The majority of neocloud companies will NOT survive. I strongly believe we're going to see a MASSIVE amount of consolidation across this industry over the next several years, and only a handful of companies will come out on top," Melvin said.

"Personally, I think $CRWV and $NBIS will be the top 2," he said.

Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, whose company is CoreWeave's second-largest investor with an approximately 10% stake, sought to reassure investors about its financial position.

"CoreWeave’s financial strength is improving every day," Huang told reporters at an event in Stockholm, adding that he did not see a need for Nvidia to backstop the company.

"I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."

Analysts see buying opportunity

Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated its Overweight rating on CoreWeave, with a $176 price target implying upside of more than 150% from its reference price.

The firm said CoreWeave had public support from Nvidia and had sold nearly all the capacity scheduled to come online in 2027.

Nvidia has an agreement to backstop any unsold capacity.

According to Cantor Fitzgerald, the principal concern is whether CoreWeave can finance the capital expenditure required to meet demand, rather than whether demand for AI computing exists.

The firm described the current period as an attractive opportunity to add to or initiate a position in the shares.

Deutsche Bank also maintained its Buy rating on CoreWeave, with a $150 price target, implying upside of more than 100% from its reference price.

Analyst Brad Zelnick acknowledged that the company's prospects are closely tied to the performance of the AI sector and demand for computing infrastructure.

He argued, however, that its underlying contracts provide meaningful support.

“The vast majority of CoreWeave’s backlog is associated with long-term take-or-pay contracts where contracted revenue fully covers all capital and operating costs associated with the contract and generates a return for the company,” Zelnick wrote.

He estimated that 60% to 65% of CoreWeave's backlog was tied to investment-grade customers at the end of the second quarter.

The company has used these contracts to secure project-specific debt at costs at or below its parent company's borrowing rate.

“A strong customer base, established record of execution, backlog conversion and leading infrastructure performance is all supportive of their issuer profile relative to neocloud peers, in our view,” Zelnick said.

Deutsche Bank also highlighted CoreWeave's financing arrangements and liquidity position.

“Available liquidity stood at $15.5 billion, and since that time the company: closed a $2.6 billion DDTL 5.5 (backed by shorter 3-yr contracts) at SOFR + 5.50%; closed a $4.2 billion 2.875% Convertible Senior Note and announced a 35 million share ATM equity program,” the bank said.

Capital needs remain a key risk

Despite the positive assessment of its customer contracts, CoreWeave faces substantial funding requirements as it expands its infrastructure.

Deutsche Bank forecasts operating cash flow of about $10 billion over the next 12 months, compared with required capital expenditure of roughly $45 billion.

That gap means the company will need to secure additional funding, although Zelnick argued it could raise capital at a steady pace, supported by its contracted customer backlog.

The central question for investors is whether CoreWeave can convert its substantial order book into cash flow quickly enough to support its expansion without putting further pressure on its balance sheet.

For now, bullish analysts see long-term contracts, investment-grade customers and Nvidia's support as reasons to look beyond the recent sell-off.

More cautious investors remain focused on the cost of financing the infrastructure boom and the risks of relying on future demand to justify heavy borrowing.

data.title: Dow opens 240 pts higher as AI stocks slide and inflation concerns weigh
data.description:
US stocks opened mixed on Friday as renewed selling in technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks weighed on sentiment, while gains in Tesla offered some support.

Investors also assessed persistent inflation pressures and the outlook for Federal Reserve interest rates ahead of the central bank’s October policy meeting.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 242 points while the S&P 500 gained 0.11%. The Nasdaq composite fell 0.28%.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for weekly losses, while the Dow remained positioned for a weekly advance.

Tesla rises as AI stocks face renewed selling

Tesla shares climbed around 0.8% in trading after the electric vehicle maker unveiled its redesigned Roadster, developed in collaboration with SpaceX and featuring rocket-style thrusters.

The vehicle is not expected to enter production until 2028.

SpaceX shares fell 2.5%.

Gains in Tesla contrasted with continued weakness across several AI-related stocks.

Nvidia-backed data centre operator CoreWeave fell 6.6% in trading, reversing some of Thursday’s rebound, as concerns about its debt burden persisted.

The company’s bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Other neocloud companies, including Nebius Group and Iren, declined more than 5% each. Micron Technology shares fell 3.6%, while Intel dropped 2.18%.

Semiconductor stocks have also faced pressure amid concerns about growing Chinese competition in the memory chip market.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF fell 1.7% in trading and was down 8.9% for the week.

The declines reflect investor concerns that data centre operators may struggle to generate profits quickly enough to service their debt, particularly if borrowing costs rise.

David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, said the pullback in memory chip stocks and concerns over CoreWeave’s debt had given investors a reason to reduce exposure to companies linked to AI.

“There’s still some caution out there,” Morrison said.

"Just a touch of profit-taking after yesterday’s rebound, or something more serious? Time will tell. But it could be argued that investor behaviour since the middle of this week could provide some insight into the future.", he added.

Inflation and Fed outlook weigh on sentiment

Investors also remained focused on hotter-than-expected inflation data released this week.

US consumer and producer prices have shown persistent pressure, with wholesale inflation recording its biggest increase since 2022 and consumer inflation remaining above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target.

Elevated energy prices following the US-Iran war have added to inflation concerns, complicating the outlook for monetary policy.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok, said the US economy remained resilient and was benefiting from an AI-driven investment boom.

He also noted that stronger spending was contributing to inflation, without offering a clear signal on the Fed’s next policy decision.

Markets increasingly expect the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting. The CME Group’s FedWatch tool indicated an 85% probability of a hold.

Morrison also pointed to sharp movements in Treasury yields as a potential signal of changing investor sentiment.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.30% on Wednesday before falling to a three-week low on Thursday.

He said the moves could reflect concerns about a possible unwinding of the AI trade or a shift towards safer assets.

Netflix and other stocks move in trading

Among other individual stocks, Varonis Systems gained 2.7% after Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint agreed to acquire the data security company in an all-cash deal valued at $6.3 billion.

Netflix shares declined 1.7% after the streaming company appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer, replacing Bela Bajaria.

Meanwhile, concerns about AI financing costs also extended to private companies.

Reuters reported that some current and prospective investors in Anthropic’s planned initial public offering were considering a lower valuation amid worries about rising AI funding costs.
